scenes.name: SC 1 · INT. TUNING WORKSHOP / STREET · NIGHT
scenes.summary: Vir gets an urgent late call to tune a piano at a mansion outside town and rides out.

shots.action: Vir wipes down a piano key in his small workshop, lit by a single lamp, when his phone buzzes.
He answers; a woman's voice says the piano must be ready by morning, and gives an address.
Vir hesitates, checking the clock — it is well past a reasonable hour to be called.
He packs his tuning kit into a worn leather satchel.
He locks up the workshop, the sign swinging in the wind.
Vir kicks his scooter to life on the empty street.
Wide of the scooter's headlight shrinking into the dark road out of town.

scenes.name: SC 2 · EXT./INT. SCOOTER / ROAD · NIGHT
scenes.summary: Riding out, Vir remembers his late teacher's advice, then arrives at the gate.

shots.action: Close on Vir's face lit by passing streetlights, lost in thought.
Flash of memory: an old man's hands pressing a single piano key, half-lit.
The old man's remembered voice: "A room remembers what a person forgets."
Vir blinks back to the present as the mansion's gate appears ahead.

scenes.name: SC 3 · INT. THE MANSION · NIGHT
scenes.summary: Let in by the caretaker, Vir finds the piano, begins tuning, and hears an answering note.

shots.action: Vir parks outside the gate, wide of the mansion looming in the dark.
He knocks on a heavy wooden door.
Nayan, the caretaker, opens the door with a single lantern.
Vir steps into a dust-sheeted hallway lined with covered furniture.
Nayan leads him past a wall of framed photographs, most turned to face the wall.
Close on the one photograph left facing out: a young woman seated at a piano.
Vir asks who she is; Nayan only says to hurry, the piano is this way.
They pass a locked door with a chain across it.
Vir is shown into the music room, dust sheets pulled off in a cloud.
The grand piano stands uncovered, already waiting, its lid open.
Nayan leaves a single candle and exits without another word.
Vir opens his kit and lays out his tools on the piano's felt.
He strikes the first key; the note rings out flat and hollow.
He adjusts a tuning pin, listening with his whole body.
A faint answering note drifts in from somewhere else in the house.
Vir freezes, tuning fork still ringing in his hand.
He strikes the same key again; the answering note comes back, closer this time.
Vir rises from the bench and turns toward the dark hallway.

scenes.name: SC 4 · INT. MANSION HALLWAYS · CONTINUOUS
scenes.summary: Candle in hand, Vir follows the answering note up through the house.

shots.action: Vir steps into the corridor, candle in hand, following the sound.
He passes the locked, chained door again, pausing at it.
The note sounds again, further down the hall, and he moves on.
He climbs a narrow staircase, the candle flame guttering.
At the top he finds a second, smaller door left ajar.
He pushes it open onto a narrow set of steps leading up into darkness.
Vir climbs, the sound growing clearer with every step.

scenes.name: SC 5 · INT. ATTIC MUSIC ROOM · NIGHT
scenes.summary: Vir finds a second piano and meets Mrs. Kapadia, who tells him about her daughter Leela.

shots.action: Vir reaches the top and finds a small attic room, untouched by dust sheets.
A second, smaller piano sits under a single skylight.
Sheet music sits open on the stand, mid-piece, as if someone just stepped away.
He touches a key; it rings the exact note that has been calling him.
Behind him, an unfamiliar voice: "That was my daughter's room."
Vir turns to find an elderly woman, Mrs. Kapadia, standing in the doorway.
She steps in, running a hand along the small piano's lid.
She explains: her daughter played every night here, until the night she didn't.
A photograph on the wall shows the young woman from downstairs, now named: Leela.
Mrs. Kapadia admits she has kept every room in the house sealed for years, except this one.
She asks Vir to finish what he came to do — tune the piano downstairs, properly this time.
Vir looks between the two pianos, understanding passing over his face.
He nods and picks up his tuning fork again.

scenes.name: SC 6 · INT. MANSION MUSIC ROOM · NIGHT
scenes.summary: Vir finishes tuning the grand piano properly while Mrs. Kapadia listens.

shots.action: Back at the grand piano, Vir works with new care, unhurried.
Mrs. Kapadia sits nearby, listening, the sheet pulled off one chair.
Vir tightens the last pin and strikes a full chord.
The chord rings true and clean through the whole house.
Mrs. Kapadia closes her eyes, a small smile breaking through.
Vir closes the piano lid gently, the work done.

scenes.name: SC 7 · INT. MANSION FOYER · NIGHT
scenes.summary: Vir is paid, given the attic's sheet music, and shown out into the night.

shots.action: Vir packs his tools back into the satchel by lamplight.
Mrs. Kapadia presses an envelope of payment into his hands.
She adds a second item: the sheet music from the attic, folded.
Vir accepts it without a word, understanding what it means.
Nayan holds the front door open for him.
Vir steps out into air that feels lighter than when he arrived.

scenes.name: SC 8 · EXT. MANSION DRIVEWAY · NIGHT
scenes.summary: Vir crosses the misted driveway as one last note hangs in the air behind him.

shots.action: From Vir's point of view, mist rolls low across the driveway.
A single note seems to hang in the fog behind him, then fades.
He does not look back, walking on into the mist toward his scooter.

scenes.name: SC 9 · INT. TUNING WORKSHOP · SUNRISE
scenes.summary: Vir wakes at his own workbench with the attic's sheet music still beside him.

shots.action: Vir wakes at his workbench, the folded sheet music beside him.
Morning light cuts through the workshop's dusty window.
He unfolds the sheet music and studies the handwritten notes on it.
He sets it upright on his own piano's stand.
He rubs his eyes, unsure how much of the night was real.

scenes.name: SC 10 · INT./EXT. TUNING WORKSHOP / STREET · DAY
scenes.summary: Vir plays Leela's piece by ear on his own piano as the film ends on credits.

shots.action: Vir opens the workshop shutters to the morning street.
He sits at his own piano for the first time in years.
He finds the opening notes of Leela's piece by ear.
His hands settle into the melody, unhurried.
Through the window, the street goes about its morning, unaware.
Vir plays on, the smallest smile on his face.
Fade out to studio credit, title card and final credits.
